body:
### Summary

Thanks for shipping Developer ID-signed, notarized macOS binaries in 0.12.12. The signatures use a different code-signing **Identifier** in every release, though. The Team ID stays `2DC432GLL2`, but the Identifier looks like the linker-generated `uv-<hash>`:

| Release | `uv` Identifier | `uvx` Identifier |
|---|---|---|
| 0.12.12 | `uv-924a20a6cc8daa66` | `uvx-52a8c5d340e3db83` |
| 0.12.24 | `uv-7d60a5a1146de3cd` | `uvx-462788ef10328e23` |
| 0.13.1 | `uv-12607afb3fd970b7` | `uvx-1704e7899e715f4e` |

(`codesign -dv` on `uv-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` contents, macOS, 2026-10-15.)

The designated requirement embeds that Identifier (`identifier "uv-12607afb3fd970b7" and anchor apple generic and ... certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "2DC432GLL2"`). So each upgrade's requirement no longer matches what earlier releases had.

### Why it matters

Tools that identify signed programs by Team ID plus Identifier treat every uv release as a different program. Little Snitch is one example: its code ID is `TEAMID/Identifier` (https://help.obdev.at/littlesnitch6/adv-code-identity). The same goes for anything that pins a designated requirement, such as MDM/PPPC profiles and allowlists. Users get a "program identity changed" prompt after every `uv self update` or reinstall, and rules or profiles have to be rewritten. A stable Identifier would let these rules survive upgrades, which is one of the benefits the signing work was meant to deliver.

### Suggestion

Sign with an explicit, stable identifier, e.g. `codesign --identifier sh.astral.uv` / `sh.astral.uvx`, or `rcodesign sign --binary-identifier ...`. Today the linker's ad-hoc identifier is kept during re-signing. The wheel-packaged binaries would benefit the same way.
title: macOS release binaries: use a stable code-signing Identifier for uv and uvx
